card.title: How To Diagnose & Fix an iPhone 7 That Does Not Charge, Takes 0.006A via USB

source.title: How To Diagnose & Fix an iPhone 7 That Does Not Charge, Takes 0.006A via USB

claims.statement: An iPhone 7 / 7 Plus that turns on but draws only about 0.006–0.007 A from USB with known-good port and battery usually has a bad Tristar U4001 (610A3B).
No draw before power-on but a first boot step of about 0.150–0.250 A on a DC supply points to Tristar; draw before power-on means a board short instead.
With only the charge flex connected and USB plugged in, about 3.7 V at battery connector J2201 is normal; under about 2 V (often 0.3–0.6 V) means bad Tristar.
After a good Tristar swap: USB charge around 1 A or more, first boot step about 0.045 A, about 3.7 V at J2201.
Tristar is partly under a shield; remove and fit it at an angle rather than cutting the shield, which can later pierce the charging port.
If still not charging, TRISTAR_BYPASS cap C4005 (1.0 µF 6.3 V 0201) may be shorted to ground.
Tristar testers (Smartmod Pro, ICC Pro, JC) reliably flag a fail but a pass does not prove Tristar is good.

procedure: Test with known-good port flex and battery outside the housing; read the USB meter.
On DC supply check draw before and after power-on.
Optionally check Tristar heating with thermal camera/freeze spray.
Measure J2201 voltage with only the charge flex connected.
Replace Tristar 610A3B at an angle under the shield; re-run all checks.
If unresolved check C4005 and diode-mode Tristar pads against boardview.

measurements.point: First boot step after power-on (bad Tristar)
J2201 battery connector, charge flex only

cautions: SOURCE RISK: Cutting the Tristar shield leaves sharp edges that can damage the charge port flex.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
